subproblem.title: Countable C¹ bi-Lipschitz chart cover of a countably n-rectifiable set (Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 and Remark 1.3)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let M ⊆ ℝ^P (ℝᵏ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)) be countably n-rectifiable in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, 1.1 (SimonGMT `CountablyRectifiable n M`: there are M₀ ⊆ ℝ^P with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, j ∈ ℕ, with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ); Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then there are maps Φ_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P of class C¹ and open sets Ω_j ⊆ ℝⁿ (j ∈ ℕ) such that each Φ_j is Lipschitz on Ω_j (with some constant K_j ≥ 0), each Φ_j is antilipschitz on Ω_j (there is c_j > 0 with c_j|w − w′| ≤ |Φ_j(w) − Φ_j(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω_j), and Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_j Φ_j(Ω_j)) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Eucl P)), CountablyRectifiable n M → ∃ (Φ : ℕ → Eucl n → Eucl P) (Ω : ℕ → Set (Eucl n)), (∀ j, IsOpen (Ω j)) ∧ (∀ j, ContDiff ℝ 1 (Φ j)) ∧ (∀ j, ∃ K : ℝ≥0, LipschitzOnWith K (Φ j) (Ω j)) ∧ (∀ j, ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω j, ∀ w' ∈ Ω j, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ j w - Φ j w'‖) ∧ (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) (M \ ⋃ j, Φ j '' Ω j) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝᵏ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with Euclidean norm |·| and inner product ⟨·,·⟩; Lⁿ := volume on ℝⁿ; Hⁿ := μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalised n-dimensional Hausdorff measure; on ℝⁿ it equals Lⁿ by Mathlib `EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`). A map Ψ is c-antilipschitz on a set S if c|w − w′| ≤ |Ψ(w) − Ψ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ S. SimonGMT `CountablyRectifiable n M` (Simon Ch. 3, 1.1) means: there are M₀ ⊆ ℝ^P with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P (j ∈ ℕ) with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ). This lemma is Step 1 of the parent proof: Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 (“only if”; the printed proof is followed in steps 4–5) together with Remark 1.3 (passage to countably many coordinate patches, done in steps 6–7 with bi-Lipschitz rational balls). The C¹ Approximation Theorem used by the printed proof is Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5; its printed proof is reproduced in step 2.

(N) Null images. If Ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P is Λ-Lipschitz on a set S ⊆ ℝⁿ then Hⁿ(Ψ(S)) ≤ Λⁿ Hⁿ(S) (SimonGMT `Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn`); hence Ψ maps Lⁿ-null subsets of S to Hⁿ-null sets.

1. (Case n = 0.) ℝ⁰ = {0}. Write M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ⁰) with H⁰(M₀) = 0. Put Φ_j := F_j and Ω_j := ℝ⁰ (open). Every map on the one-point space ℝ⁰ is constant, hence C¹, 0-Lipschitz and 1-antilipschitz (both sides of the antilipschitz inequality are 0). Since M ∖ ⋃_j Φ_j(Ω_j) ⊆ M₀, we get H⁰(M ∖ ⋃_j Φ_j(Ω_j)) = 0. From now on n ≥ 1 (the argument below is also valid for n = 0).

2. (C¹ Approximation Theorem, Simon Ch. 2, 1.5; printed proof.) Claim: if g : ℝⁿ → ℝ is Lipschitz and ε > 0, there are a closed A ⊆ ℝⁿ with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A) < ε and h ∈ C¹(ℝⁿ) with h = g on A.
 (a) By Rademacher's theorem (Mathlib `LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt`) the set B := {x : g is differentiable at x}, which is Borel (Mathlib `measurableSet_of_differentiableAt`), satisfies Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ B) = 0. The map Dg := fderiv ℝ g : ℝⁿ → L(ℝⁿ, ℝ) is Borel (Mathlib `measurable_fderiv`), and ‖Dg(x)‖ ≤ Lip g for every x.
 (b) (Lusin, also on sets of infinite measure.) For a ≥ 1 let S_a := {x : a − 1 ≤ |x| < a} (bounded Borel annuli). Lusin's theorem for the finite measure Lⁿ⌞(S_a ∩ B) (SimonGMT `Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable` applied to the n coordinates x ↦ Dg(x)(e_i), intersecting the resulting closed sets) gives a closed C_a ⊆ S_a ∩ B with Dg|C_a continuous and Lⁿ((S_a ∩ B) ∖ C_a) < ε/2^{a+3}. Put C := ⋃_a C_a. Every bounded set meets only finitely many S_a, hence finitely many C_a; so C is closed (locally finite union of closed sets) and Dg|C is continuous (near each point C is a finite union of closed sets on each of which Dg is continuous). Moreover C ⊆ B and Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ C) ≤ Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ B) + Σ_a Lⁿ((S_a ∩ B) ∖ C_a) < ε/2. (The accepted DAG lemma `lpf_c1r_lusin_closed` states exactly this for an arbitrary Borel set S ⊆ ℝⁿ, here S = B.)
 (c) For x, y ∈ C with x ≠ y put R(x,y) := (g(y) − g(x) − Dg(x)(y − x))/|y − x|; then |R(x,y)| ≤ 2 Lip g. For k ≥ 1 and x ∈ C put η_k(x) := sup{|R(x,y)| : y ∈ C, 0 < |y − x| < 1/k} (sup ∅ := 0). For fixed y, x ↦ R(x,y) is continuous on C ∖ {y} (g and Dg|C are continuous). Hence if η_k(x) > t, witnessed by some y, then η_k(x′) > t for all x′ ∈ C sufficiently close to x; so η_k is lower semicontinuous on C, hence Borel. The η_k decrease in k, and η_k(x) → 0 for every x ∈ C because g is differentiable at x ∈ C ⊆ B with derivative Dg(x).
 (d) (Egoroff.) By Egoroff's theorem (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.tendstoUniformlyOn_of_ae_tendsto`) on each finite-measure set C ∩ S_a with tolerance ε/2^{a+3} (applied to the sequence (η_k)_k), there is a measurable A₀ ⊆ C with Lⁿ(C ∖ A₀) < ε/4 such that η_k → 0 uniformly on every bounded subset of A₀ (a bounded set meets only finitely many S_a). By inner regularity of Lⁿ, again annulus by annulus, there is a closed A ⊆ A₀ with Lⁿ(A₀ ∖ A) < ε/4 (the union of the closed pieces is closed by local finiteness). Hence Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A) < ε/2 + ε/4 + ε/4 = ε. (The accepted DAG lemma `lpf_c1r_egoroff_closed` is this closed-set form of Egoroff's theorem; the accepted DAG lemma `lpf_c1r_uniform_remainder` packages (c)–(d) together with the Whitney condition of (e): for Lipschitz g, closed C on which g is differentiable with Dg|C continuous, and ε > 0, it yields a closed A ⊆ C with Lⁿ(C ∖ A) < ε satisfying that condition.)
 (e) (Whitney.) g|A and Dg|A are continuous. If K ⊆ A is compact and δ > 0, choose k with sup_K η_k < δ (K is bounded); then for x ∈ K and y ∈ A with 0 < |y − x| < 1/k: |g(y) − g(x) − Dg(x)(y − x)| = |R(x,y)| |y − x| ≤ η_k(x)|y − x| ≤ δ|y − x|. This is Whitney's condition (Simon Ch. 2, 1.6(‡)). By Whitney's Extension Theorem (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.6; proof in [EG92, §6.5] or [Fed69, 3.1.14]; in Lean it is the accepted DAG lemma `lpf_c1r_whitney_extension`, whose hypotheses are exactly: A closed, g and Dg continuous on A, and the compact-uniform remainder estimate just proved) there is h ∈ C¹(ℝⁿ) with h = g on A (and Dh = Dg on A). □

3. (Vector-valued version.) Let F : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be Lipschitz and ε > 0. If P = 0 put G :≡ 0 and A := ℝⁿ. Otherwise apply step 2 to each coordinate F^l := ⟨F, e_l⟩ (Lipschitz), l = 1, …, P, with ε/P, obtaining closed A_l and h_l ∈ C¹(ℝⁿ) with h_l = F^l on A_l; put A := ⋂_l A_l (closed, Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A) ≤ Σ_l Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A_l) < ε) and G := Σ_l h_l e_l ∈ C¹(ℝⁿ; ℝ^P). Then F = G on A.

4. (Simon's proof of Lemma 1.2: reduction to C¹ maps.) By hypothesis M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_{j∈ℕ} F_j(ℝⁿ) with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and each F_j Lipschitz. For j ∈ ℕ and i ≥ 1, step 3 gives G_{ij} ∈ C¹(ℝⁿ; ℝ^P) and a closed A_{ij} with F_j = G_{ij} on A_{ij} and Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A_{ij}) < 1/i. Put Z_j := ℝⁿ ∖ ⋃_i A_{ij}. Then Lⁿ(Z_j) ≤ 1/i for every i, so Lⁿ(Z_j) = 0, and E_j := F_j(Z_j) satisfies Hⁿ(E_j) = 0 by (N). If w ∉ Z_j then w ∈ A_{ij} for some i and F_j(w) = G_{ij}(w). Hence
 (1) M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j E_j ∪ ⋃_{i,j} G_{ij}(ℝⁿ).

5. (Critical points have Hⁿ-null image; Simon: “by the area formula …{x : JG_{ij} = 0}…”.) Fix G := G_{ij} and let Crit := {w ∈ ℝⁿ : DG(w) is not injective}. The set of injective linear maps ℝⁿ → ℝ^P is open in L(ℝⁿ, ℝ^P): if A is injective there is m > 0 with |As| ≥ m|s| for all s (finite dimension; any m > 0 works when n = 0), and then every B with ‖B − A‖ < m satisfies |Bs| ≥ (m − ‖B − A‖)|s|, so B is injective. Since DG is continuous, Crit is closed, hence Borel. G is differentiable at every point. By the area formula in the form of SimonGMT `Chapter02.area_image_eq_zero_of_critical` (for a Borel set s on which a map ℝⁿ → ℝ^P is differentiable with non-injective derivative, the Hⁿ-measure of the image of s is 0; here finrank ℝ ℝⁿ = n), Hⁿ(G(Crit)) = 0.

6. (Regular points: bi-Lipschitz balls; inverse-function argument.) Let w₀ ∈ ℝⁿ ∖ Crit and A := DG(w₀). As A is an injective linear map on the finite-dimensional space ℝⁿ, there is m > 0 with |As| ≥ m|s| for all s ∈ ℝⁿ. Put c := m/2. By continuity of DG choose r > 0 with ‖DG(z) − A‖ ≤ c for |z − w₀| < r. For z, z′ in the convex ball B_r(w₀), the mean value inequality applied to z ↦ G(z) − Az gives |G(z) − G(z′) − A(z − z′)| ≤ c|z − z′|, hence |G(z) − G(z′)| ≥ m|z − z′| − c|z − z′| = c|z − z′|; and since ‖DG‖ ≤ ‖A‖ + c on B_r(w₀), the mean value inequality also gives |G(z) − G(z′)| ≤ (‖A‖ + c)|z − z′|. (Accepted DAG lemma `lpf_c1_local_antilipschitz` is the antilipschitz part.) Choose an open ball O with rational centre and rational radius with w₀ ∈ O ⊆ B_r(w₀); G is Lipschitz and c-antilipschitz on O. Let 𝒪_{ij} be the countable set of open balls O with rational centre and rational radius such that G_{ij} is Lipschitz on O (with some constant) and c-antilipschitz on O for some c > 0. We have shown ℝⁿ ∖ Crit_{ij} ⊆ ⋃_{O∈𝒪_{ij}} O, so
 (2) G_{ij}(ℝⁿ) ⊆ G_{ij}(Crit_{ij}) ∪ ⋃_{O∈𝒪_{ij}} G_{ij}(O).

7. (The charts.) Let 𝒯 be the countable set of triples (i, j, O) with i ≥ 1, j ∈ ℕ and O ∈ 𝒪_{ij}. If 𝒯 = ∅ put Φ_k :≡ 0 and Ω_k := ∅ for all k ∈ ℕ (∅ is open, constants are C¹, and the Lipschitz and antilipschitz conditions on ∅ hold vacuously, e.g. with constants 0 and 1). Otherwise choose a surjection k ↦ (i_k, j_k, O_k) from ℕ onto 𝒯 and put Φ_k := G_{i_k j_k}, Ω_k := O_k. In both cases every Ω_k is open, every Φ_k is C¹ on ℝⁿ (`ContDiff ℝ 1`), Lipschitz on Ω_k and antilipschitz on Ω_k with a positive constant, and ⋃_k Φ_k(Ω_k) = ⋃_{(i,j,O)∈𝒯} G_{ij}(O).

8. (Conclusion.) By (1) and (2), M ∖ ⋃_k Φ_k(Ω_k) ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j E_j ∪ ⋃_{i,j} G_{ij}(Crit_{ij}), a countable union of Hⁿ-null sets (hypothesis, step 4 and step 5). By countable subadditivity Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_k Φ_k(Ω_k)) = 0, which together with step 7 is the claim. ∎

subproblem.title: Weighted approximate tangent plane of (M, θ) along a C¹ antilipschitz chart (Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6 ⟹, Remarks 1.5(2), 1.8(1))
subproblem.statement: Let Q, n ∈ ℕ (ℝᵏ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), Hⁿ = μHE[n]), V ⊆ ℝ^Q open, M ⊆ V Hⁿ-null-measurable, and θ : ℝ^Q → ℝ with θ(y) > 0 for y ∈ M and θ Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ V. Let Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ be open and Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q of class C¹ such that for some c > 0, c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω. Then for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M ∩ Φ(Ω) and every w ∈ Ω with Φ(w) = y, the subspace DΦ(w)(ℝⁿ) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Φ w) is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at y in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, 1.7, i.e. HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y (DΦ(w)(ℝⁿ)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (V M : Set (Eucl Q)) (θ : Eucl Q → ℝ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl Q) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)), IsOpen V → M ⊆ V → NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) → (∀ y ∈ M, 0 < θ y) → (∀ K : Set (Eucl Q), IsCompact K → K ⊆ V → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ K) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q))) → IsOpen Ω → ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → ∀ᵐ y ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)).restrict (M ∩ Φ '' Ω)), ∀ w ∈ Ω, Φ w = y → HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Φ w).toLinearMap)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝᵏ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), |·| Euclidean norm, ⟨·,·⟩ inner product; Lⁿ := volume on ℝⁿ; Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^Q (translation invariant; Hⁿ(λS) = λⁿHⁿ(S) for λ > 0, Mathlib `MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀`; Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ). B_ρ(y), B̄_ρ(y) are the open and closed balls. η_{y,r}(x) := r⁻¹(x − y) (SimonGMT `blowUpMap y r`), r > 0. By definition, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y T means: dim T = n and, for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q), ∫_{η_{y,r}(M)} φ(z) θ(y + rz) dHⁿ(z) → θ(y) ∫_T φ dHⁿ as r ↓ 0; SimonGMT `HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y T` (Simon 1.4) is the same with θ ≡ 1 and S in place of M. Put N := Φ(Ω). This lemma is the existence half of Step 6 of the parent proof, which cites Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2), the proof of Theorem 1.6 “⟹” and Remark 1.8(1) (weighted version); those printed arguments are copied below, specialised to the single C¹ chart N, with all details filled in. (The parent's parenthetical treats the term θ − θ(y) on M ∩ N via Lebesgue points; following the cited Remark 1.8(1), the same estimate is obtained from compact Lusin pieces C on which θ is continuous, steps 1–4.)

0. Preliminaries on the chart.
 (a) Let w ∈ Ω, s ∈ ℝⁿ. For small |t|, w + ts ∈ Ω (Ω open), so c|t||s| ≤ |Φ(w + ts) − Φ(w)|; dividing by |t| and letting t → 0 gives c|s| ≤ |DΦ(w)s|. Hence DΦ(w) is injective and T_w := DΦ(w)(ℝⁿ) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Φ w) has dimension n. Φ is injective on Ω (Φ(w) = Φ(w′) forces c|w − w′| ≤ 0). For y ∈ N let w_y denote the unique point of Ω with Φ(w_y) = y; the clause “∀ w ∈ Ω, Φ w = y → …” of the claim only concerns w = w_y. Put T_y := T_{w_y}. The inverse Ψ := (Φ|Ω)⁻¹ : N → Ω is c⁻¹-Lipschitz.
 (b) N is σ-compact (Ω is a countable union of compact sets and Φ is continuous), hence Borel; so M ∩ N is Hⁿ-null-measurable.
 (c) (N is locally Hⁿ-finite.) Let K ⊆ ℝ^Q be compact. Ψ(N ∩ K) has diameter ≤ c⁻¹ diam K, so it lies in a closed ball B̄ ⊆ ℝⁿ. Φ is Λ-Lipschitz on the compact convex set B̄, Λ := max_{B̄}‖DΦ‖ (mean value inequality; Φ is C¹). Hence Hⁿ(N ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(Φ(B̄)) ≤ Λⁿ Lⁿ(B̄) < ∞ (SimonGMT `Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn`).
 (d) (Blow-up change of variables.) η_{y,r} is a translation followed by the dilation by r⁻¹, so for every set S ⊆ ℝ^Q and every g : ℝ^Q → ℝ, ∫_{η_{y,r}(S)} g dHⁿ = r^{−n} ∫_S g(η_{y,r}(x)) dHⁿ(x) (Bochner integrals; this is the accepted DAG lemma `lpf_wtc_blowup_setIntegral_image`), and Hⁿ(η_{y,r}(S) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = r^{−n} Hⁿ(S ∩ B̄_{rR}(y)).
 (e) (C¹ blow-up of N; Simon: “since x ∈ N_j and N_j is a C¹ submanifold, lim ∫_{η_{x,λ}(N_j)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{T_x N_j} f dHⁿ”.) Claim: for every y ∈ N and φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q), ∫_{η_{y,r}(N)} φ dHⁿ → ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ as r ↓ 0 (so N has approximate tangent space T_y at y), and for every R > 0, sup_{0<r≤1} r^{−n} Hⁿ(N ∩ B̄_{rR}(y)) < ∞.
 Proof. Let w := w_y, spt φ ⊆ B_R(0), 0 < r ≤ 1. By (d), ∫_{η(N)} φ dHⁿ = r^{−n} ∫_N φ((x − y)/r) dHⁿ(x). If the integrand is nonzero at x then x = Φ(v) with v ∈ Ω and |Φ(v) − Φ(w)| < rR, hence c|v − w| < rR and |v − w| < R/c. Let Ω′ := Ω ∩ B_{R/c+1}(w): a bounded open set on which Φ is injective and Lipschitz (argument of (c)). By the injective area formula (Simon Ch. 2, (3.5); SimonGMT `Chapter02.injective_area_formula_lipschitzOn`, and in weighted form `Chapter02.weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn` applied to a global Lipschitz extension of Φ|Ω′, which agrees with Φ on the open set Ω′ and so has the same derivative there; applied to φ⁺ and φ⁻ separately), with the area Jacobian JΦ(v) := √det(⟨DΦ(v)e_i, DΦ(v)e_j⟩)_{i,j} (this equals SimonGMT's area Jacobian normDet DΦ(v), by Mathlib `LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram` for the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ together with `LinearMap.normDet_nonneg`),
 r^{−n} ∫_N φ((x − y)/r) dHⁿ(x) = r^{−n} ∫_{Ω′} φ((Φ(v) − Φ(w))/r) JΦ(v) dv = ∫_{ℝⁿ} 1_{Ω′}(w + rs) φ((Φ(w + rs) − Φ(w))/r) JΦ(w + rs) ds,
 the last step by the substitution v = w + rs (dv = rⁿ ds). The last integrand vanishes for |s| ≥ R/c and is bounded by sup|φ| · max_{|z−w|≤R/c} JΦ(z) < ∞ (JΦ is continuous since DΦ is; accepted DAG lemma `lpf_wtc_cat_gram_jacobian_continuous`). For fixed s, as r ↓ 0: w + rs ∈ Ω′ eventually (Ω′ open), (Φ(w + rs) − Φ(w))/r → DΦ(w)s, and JΦ(w + rs) → JΦ(w). By dominated convergence the integral tends to JΦ(w) ∫_{ℝⁿ} φ(DΦ(w)s) ds (this limit is the accepted DAG lemma `lpf_wtc_cat_rescaled_integral_tendsto`), which equals ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ by the area formula for the injective linear (hence Lipschitz) map s ↦ DΦ(w)s, whose Jacobian is the constant JΦ(w). For the density bound, take φ₀ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q) with 1_{B̄_R(0)} ≤ φ₀ ≤ 1_{B_{2R}(0)}; the same identity (with 2R in place of R) gives r^{−n} Hⁿ(N ∩ B̄_{rR}(y)) = Hⁿ(η(N) ∩ B̄_R(0)) ≤ ∫_{η(N)} φ₀ dHⁿ ≤ max_{|z−w|≤2R/c} JΦ(z) · Lⁿ(B_{2R/c}(0)) for all 0 < r ≤ 1. □
 (f) (Upper Density Theorem, Simon Ch. 1, 3.6 with Remark 3.7(2); SimonGMT `Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6`.) Let W ⊆ ℝ^Q be open, S ⊆ ℝ^Q Hⁿ-null-measurable and g : ℝ^Q → [0, ∞] with ∫_{S∩K} g dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ W. Then for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ W ∖ S, ρ^{−n} ∫_{S ∩ B̄_ρ(y)} g dHⁿ → 0 as ρ ↓ 0. Proof: cover W by countably many open balls B with closure B ⊆ W; μ_B := g·Hⁿ⌞(S ∩ B) is a finite Borel (hence Borel regular) measure, so by 3.6 its upper n-density vanishes at Hⁿ-a.e. point outside S ∩ B; for y ∈ B ∖ S and small ρ, B̄_ρ(y) ⊆ B, so μ_B(B̄_ρ(y)) = ∫_{S ∩ B̄_ρ(y)} g dHⁿ. The constant ω_n and the positive factor between Simon's Hⁿ and μHE[n] change neither null sets nor the vanishing of the limit. (This is the accepted DAG lemma `lpf_wtc_ae_zero_density_off_set`.)

1. (Compact pieces with continuous weight; Remark 1.8(1).) There are compact C_k ⊆ M (k ∈ ℕ) with θ|C_k continuous, Hⁿ(C_k) < ∞ and Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_k C_k) = 0. (The accepted DAG lemma `lpf_wtc_lusin_compact_pieces` has exactly this statement.) Proof: let V_i (i ≥ 1) be open sets with compact closures closure V_i ⊆ V and ⋃_i V_i = V (e.g. V_i := {x ∈ V : |x| < i, dist(x, ℝ^Q ∖ V) > 1/i}). Fix i. θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ closure V_i, so there are a Borel function θ_i and a Borel set M_i′ ⊆ M ∩ V_i with Hⁿ((M ∩ V_i) ∖ M_i′) = 0 and θ = θ_i on M_i′ (M is Hⁿ-null-measurable); θ_i > 0 on M_i′ because θ > 0 on M. ν_i(B) := ∫_{B ∩ M_i′} θ_i dHⁿ is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^Q, hence closed- and compact-inner regular. For j ≥ 1, Lusin's theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; SimonGMT `Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable`, applicable because ν_i is finite and closed-inner regular) gives a closed C_{i,j} ⊆ M_i′ with ν_i(M_i′ ∖ C_{i,j}) < 1/j and θ_i|C_{i,j} continuous. C_{i,j} is closed and contained in the compact set closure V_i, hence compact; C_{i,j} ⊆ M, and θ|C_{i,j} = θ_i|C_{i,j} is continuous; so ν_i(M_i′ ∖ ⋃_j C_{i,j}) = 0, and since θ_i > 0 on M_i′, Hⁿ(M_i′ ∖ ⋃_j C_{i,j}) = 0, whence Hⁿ((M ∩ V_i) ∖ ⋃_j C_{i,j}) = 0. θ is continuous and positive on the compact C_{i,j}, so θ ≥ m > 0 there and Hⁿ(C_{i,j}) ≤ m⁻¹ ∫_{C_{i,j}} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (trivial if C_{i,j} = ∅). Since M = ⋃_i (M ∩ V_i), enumerating all C_{i,j} as C_k gives the claim.

2. (Unweighted tangent of a piece on the chart; proof of 1.6 “⟹”.) Fix C := C_k. Apply (f):
 (i) with W := ℝ^Q, S := C ∖ N, g := 1 (Hⁿ(S) ≤ Hⁿ(C) < ∞): for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C ∩ N, ρ^{−n} Hⁿ((C ∖ N) ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) → 0;
 (ii) with W := ℝ^Q, S := N ∖ C, g := 1 (locally finite by 0(c)): for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C ∩ N, ρ^{−n} Hⁿ((N ∖ C) ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) → 0.
 Let y ∈ C ∩ N satisfy (i) and (ii) and let φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q), spt φ ⊆ B_R(0), η := η_{y,r}. As η is a bijection, η(C) = η(C ∩ N) ⊔ η(C ∖ N) and η(N) = η(C ∩ N) ⊔ η(N ∖ C), all these sets are Hⁿ-measurable with locally finite measure (by (d), Hⁿ(C) < ∞ and 0(c)), and φ is bounded with compact support, so
 ∫_{η(C)} φ dHⁿ = ∫_{η(N)} φ dHⁿ − ∫_{η(N∖C)} φ dHⁿ + ∫_{η(C∖N)} φ dHⁿ.
 By (d), |∫_{η(N∖C)} φ| ≤ sup|φ| · r^{−n} Hⁿ((N ∖ C) ∩ B̄_{rR}(y)) = sup|φ| · Rⁿ (rR)^{−n} Hⁿ((N ∖ C) ∩ B̄_{rR}(y)) → 0 by (ii), and likewise |∫_{η(C∖N)} φ| → 0 by (i), while ∫_{η(N)} φ → ∫_{T_y} φ by 0(e). Hence C has approximate tangent space T_y at y (dim T_y = n by 0(a)). Moreover r^{−n} Hⁿ(C ∩ B̄_{rR}(y)) ≤ r^{−n} Hⁿ(N ∩ B̄_{rR}(y)) + r^{−n} Hⁿ((C ∖ N) ∩ B̄_{rR}(y)) is bounded for 0 < r ≤ 1 small (0(e) and (i)). (The accepted DAG lemma `lpf_wtc_density_bound_of_tangent` derives such a bound from the tangent property alone.)

3. (Remaining mass of M.) Apply (f) with W := V, S := M ∖ C, g := θ (θ ≥ 0 on M and ∫_{(M∖C)∩K} θ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ V): for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C (C ⊆ M ⊆ V and y ∉ M ∖ C), ρ^{−n} ∫_{(M∖C) ∩ B̄_ρ(y)} θ dHⁿ → 0.

4. (Weighted blow-up; Remark 1.8(1).) Let y ∈ C ∩ N satisfy the conclusions of steps 2 and 3, let φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q) with spt φ ⊆ B_R(0), and choose r₀ ∈ (0, 1] with B̄_{r₀R}(y) ⊆ V (V open). For 0 < r < r₀, by (d),
 ∫_{η(M)} φ(z) θ(y + rz) dHⁿ(z) = r^{−n} ∫_M φ(η(x)) θ(x) dHⁿ(x),
 where x ↦ φ(η(x))θ(x) vanishes off M ∩ B_{rR}(y) and is Hⁿ-integrable (|φ(η(x))θ(x)| ≤ sup|φ| θ(x) and θ is integrable on M ∩ B̄_{r₀R}(y)); also x ↦ φ(η(x)) and x ↦ φ(η(x))(θ(x) − θ(y)) are integrable on C (Hⁿ(C) < ∞, θ integrable on the compact C ⊆ M ∩ V). Splitting M = C ⊔ (M ∖ C) and writing θ = θ(y) + (θ − θ(y)) on C (accepted DAG lemma `lpf_wtc_wtt_blowup_integral_split`):
 r^{−n} ∫_M φ(η(x)) θ(x) dHⁿ(x) = I₁ + I₂ + I₃, where
 I₁ := θ(y) r^{−n} ∫_C φ(η(x)) dHⁿ(x) = θ(y) ∫_{η(C)} φ dHⁿ → θ(y) ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ (step 2 and (d));
 I₂ := r^{−n} ∫_{C ∩ B̄_{rR}(y)} φ(η(x))(θ(x) − θ(y)) dHⁿ(x), so |I₂| ≤ sup|φ| · sup_{C ∩ B̄_{rR}(y)} |θ − θ(y)| · r^{−n} Hⁿ(C ∩ B̄_{rR}(y)) → 0, because θ|C is continuous at y and the density ratio is bounded (step 2) — this is the Lebesgue-point estimate of the parent's sketch;
 I₃ := r^{−n} ∫_{(M∖C) ∩ B̄_{rR}(y)} φ(η(x)) θ(x) dHⁿ(x), so |I₃| ≤ sup|φ| · Rⁿ (rR)^{−n} ∫_{(M∖C) ∩ B̄_{rR}(y)} θ dHⁿ → 0 (step 3; accepted DAG lemma `lpf_wtc_wtt_remainder_vanishes`).
 Hence ∫_{η_{y,r}(M)} φ(z) θ(y + rz) dHⁿ(z) → θ(y) ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q); with dim T_y = n (0(a)) this is HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y T_y.

5. (Conclusion.) Let Z be the set of y ∈ M ∩ N at which the claim fails, i.e. HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y (range DΦ(w_y)) does not hold. Then Z ⊆ (M ∖ ⋃_k C_k) ∪ ⋃_k Z_k, where Z_k ⊆ C_k ∩ N is the union of the Hⁿ-null exceptional sets of steps 2(i), 2(ii) and 3 for C = C_k: indeed every y ∈ (C_k ∩ N) ∖ Z_k satisfies the claim by step 4, and w_y is the only w ∈ Ω with Φ(w) = y (0(a)). By step 1 and countable subadditivity Hⁿ(Z) = 0. As M ∩ N is Hⁿ-null-measurable (0(b)), this is exactly ∀ᵐ y ∂(Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ Φ(Ω))), ∀ w ∈ Ω, Φ(w) = y → HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Φ w)). ∎
 (For n = 0 all steps hold verbatim: ℝ⁰ is a point, H⁰ = μHE[0] is counting measure, λ⁰ = 1, N is empty or a single point and T_y = {0}.)
